# Scroll-driven Animations for Tailwind CSS

> Unofficial, experimental Tailwind CSS plugin (`@adam.plesnik/tailwindcss-scroll-driven-animations`) that adds utilities for CSS scroll-driven animations: `animation-timeline`, `scroll-timeline`, `view-timeline`, `animation-range` and `timeline-scope`, plus a `no-animations` variant for fallback styling. Version 0.4+ supports Tailwind CSS v4; version 0.3.x supports Tailwind CSS v3.4+.

The plugin does not ship any keyframes or animations. Define them as usual in Tailwind CSS (for example `--animate-*` theme variables in v4) and add the plugin's utilities to drive them by scrolling instead of time.

## Installation

Tailwind CSS v4:

```sh
npm install @adam.plesnik/tailwindcss-scroll-driven-animations
```

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@plugin '@adam.plesnik/tailwindcss-scroll-driven-animations';
```

Tailwind CSS v3.4+ (use the 0.3 release):

```sh
npm install @adam.plesnik/tailwindcss-scroll-driven-animations@0.3
```

```js
// tailwind.config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: [require('@adam.plesnik/tailwindcss-scroll-driven-animations')],
}
```

## Utilities

Timeline names are passed as a modifier after a slash and get the `--` prefix automatically: `timeline/navbar` sets `animation-timeline: --navbar`.

### Animation timeline

| Class | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `timeline` | `animation-timeline: scroll(y)` |
| `timeline-scroll-x` | `animation-timeline: scroll(x)` |
| `timeline-view` | `animation-timeline: view()` |
| `timeline-auto` | `animation-timeline: auto` |
| `timeline-none` | `animation-timeline: none` |
| `timeline/{name}` | `animation-timeline: --{name}` |

### Scroll timeline (set on the scrollable element)

| Class | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `scroll-timeline/{name}` | `scroll-timeline: --{name} y` |
| `scroll-timeline-x/{name}` | `scroll-timeline: --{name} x` |
| `scroll-timeline-block/{name}` | `scroll-timeline: --{name} block` |

### View timeline (set on the subject inside a scrollable element)

| Class | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `view-timeline/{name}` | `view-timeline: --{name} y` |
| `view-timeline-x/{name}` | `view-timeline: --{name} x` |
| `view-timeline-block/{name}` | `view-timeline: --{name} block` |

### Animation range (set on the animated element)

| Class | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `range` | `animation-range: cover 0 cover 100%` |
| `range-contain` | `animation-range: contain 0 contain 100%` |
| `range-on-entry` | `animation-range: entry 0 entry 100%` |
| `range-on-exit` | `animation-range: exit 0 exit 100%` |
| `range/{start}_{end}` | `animation-range: cover {start} cover {end}` |

The `{start}_{end}` modifier works with every range utility, for example `range-on-entry/10px_100px` sets `animation-range: entry 10px entry 100px`.

### Timeline scope

| Class | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `scope/{name}` | `timeline-scope: --{name}` |

Use it on a common ancestor so that elements outside the one defining a named timeline can use it.

### Fallback variant

| Variant | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `no-animations:*` | `@supports not (animation-range: cover) { ... }` |

## Examples

Progress bar driven by the page scroll:

```html
<div class="animate-scale-to-right timeline"></div>
```

Element that animates as it enters the viewport:

```html
<div class="animate-appear timeline-view"></div>
```

Navigation bar revealed when another element leaves the viewport, using a named view timeline shared through `scope`:

```html
<div class="scope/navbar">
  <div class="animate-translate-down timeline/navbar range-on-exit -translate-y-16 no-animations:translate-y-0">
    Navigation bar
  </div>
  <div class="view-timeline/navbar">Controlling element</div>
</div>
```

```css
@theme {
  --animate-translate-down: translate-down 3s linear forwards;

  @keyframes translate-down {
    to {
      translate: 0;
    }
  }
}
```

## Notes

- The `animation` shorthand resets `animation-timeline` to `auto`, so the timeline must be declared after the animation. Tailwind CSS outputs `animate-*` utilities before this plugin's utilities, so combining them in one `class` attribute works.
- In Tailwind CSS v4, `translate-*` utilities set the CSS `translate` property, so keyframes that undo them must animate `translate`, not `transform`.
- Scroll-driven animations are not supported in every browser yet. Use the `no-animations:` variant for fallback styles.
